base_rationale: CAM is the recommended base for 2Sa11. BOTH witnesses here transmit the FULL/LONG Bathsheba narrative with 0 illegible tokens -- this is NOT a short-vs-long recensional extent split (contrast 1Sa17). The base is chosen on cleanliness / legibility / continuity (decision D3). CAM (Cambridge UL MS Add. 1570, hi-res master) has clean parchment, excellent ink, a smooth unbroken per-verse token flow, and only 4 'damaged' tokens (all minor: a faded brown 'be'sit' v3, a column-edge 'ebew' v11, a rubbed 'em-ryo' v20, an abbreviated 'iya0bes' v24) out of 44 flags / 424 tokens (10.4%). GG, although it segments into the full 27 sense units (508 tokens, 48 flags = 9.4%), collapses across vv.15/23/25 into many abraded SINGLE-SYLLABLE fragment tokens where the scribe set a red cross-point after almost every word over worn parchment, and GG additionally carries a genuine recensional messenger DOUBLET (Joab's Abimelech/millstone/Thebez instruction repeated near-verbatim as the messenger's own delivery, GG vv.21-22) which further fragments its stream. CAM is thus the more continuous and legible witness for this chapter and the GAPS source-map's designated primary Samuel witness. CAM does not separate the equivalents of the familiar v19 and v20 (one merged sense-object, no red cross divider); the spine is nonetheless the canonical 27-verse KJV enumeration and CAM's offset sense-objects are sliced onto the correct KJV spine rows by narrative content (never positional v==v). The materially-sub-90% both-confident agreement alongside ~100% semantic pass is the honest signature of two DISTINCT full recensions of the same narrative, not a defect of either transcription.

verses.semantic_note: 2Sa11:1 -- after the year expired, when kings go forth, David sent Joab and his servants and all Israel, destroyed Ammon and besieged Rabbah, but David tarried at Jerusalem -- GG and CAM both carry the spring-war-season clause, the sending of Joab, the destruction of Ammon, the siege of Rabbah (GG 'ʿara', CAM 'Raba') and David remaining at Jerusalem.

2Sa11:2 -- in an eveningtide David arose from his bed, walked on the roof of the king's house and saw a woman washing herself, very beautiful -- both witnesses render the evening, the rising, the roof of the king's house, the seeing of the bathing woman and her beauty (CAM adds 'raʾeya fedfade', exceedingly fair to look upon).

2Sa11:3 -- David enquired after the woman; one said, Is not this Bath-sheba daughter of Eliam, wife of Uriah the Hittite -- both name Bath-sheba (ቤርሳቤሕ), the father (ኤልያብ) and Uriah the Hittite (GG እርዮ ኬጥያዊ / CAM ኦርዮ ዜጥያዊ); GG additionally has the explicit 'David sent' head clause.

2Sa11:4 -- David sent, took her, lay with her (she being purified from her uncleanness) and she returned to her house -- both carry the sending, the taking, the lying together, the purification clause and her return home.

2Sa11:5 -- the woman conceived and sent and told David, saying, I am with child -- both render the conception, the sending word to David and the message 'I am with child' (CAM explicit 'wa-zenewoto').
2Sa11:6 -- David sent to Joab, Send me Uriah the Hittite; Joab sent Uriah to David -- both carry David's order to Joab and Joab sending Uriah back; GG has a damaged plus ('nabi ye').

2Sa11:7 -- when Uriah was come, David demanded how Joab did, how the people did, how the war prospered -- both render Uriah's coming and David's threefold enquiry (welfare of Joab / of the people / of the war).

2Sa11:8 -- David said, Go down to thy house and wash thy feet; Uriah departed and a mess of meat from the king followed him -- both carry the 'go down / wash thy feet' order, Uriah leaving the king's house and the royal portion sent after him (GG ተስዕሮ ወዳሊ / CAM ተለዎ ወዓሌ).

2Sa11:9 -- Uriah slept at the door of the king's house with the servants of his lord and went not down to his house -- both render Uriah sleeping at the king's-house door with the servants and not going down home (GG terse 'wa-bete Eryo yedo'; CAM 'wa-sekebe ... weste dede').
2Sa11:10 -- they told David Uriah went not down; David asked, Camest thou not from thy journey? why didst thou not go down to thine house -- both carry the report and David's reproach to Uriah.

2Sa11:11 -- Uriah: the ark and Israel and Judah abide in tents, Joab and the servants encamp in the open field; shall I go to my house to eat, drink and lie with my wife? as thou livest I will not do this -- both render the ark/Israel/Judah-in-tents, Joab in the field, the rhetorical refusal and the oath; CAM shows the column-turn 'ebew' dittograph.

2Sa11:12 -- David: Tarry here today also, tomorrow I will let thee depart; Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day and the morrow -- both carry David's 'tarry today' and Uriah remaining; GG adds 'wa-sanita' (and the morrow).

2Sa11:13 -- David called him, he ate and drank before him and was made drunk; at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants, but went not down -- both render the feast, the making-drunk, the evening lying with the servants and not going down home.
2Sa11:14 -- in the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah -- both carry the morning, the writing of the letter to Joab and its sending by Uriah's own hand.

2Sa11:15 -- he wrote, Set Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle and retire from him, that he be smitten and die -- both render the death-letter: Uriah to the front of the strong battle, the others to retire, that he be smitten and die (GG heavily abraded but the clause-beats are all present).
2Sa11:16 -- when Joab observed the city he assigned Uriah to a place where he knew valiant men were -- both carry Joab watching the city and placing Uriah where the strong men were.

2Sa11:17 -- the men of the city went out and fought with Joab; some of David's people fell and Uriah the Hittite died also -- both render the sortie, the fighting with Joab, the fallen and Uriah's death.
2Sa11:18 -- then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war -- both carry Joab sending to report the whole matter of the war to the king.

2Sa11:19 -- and charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war unto the king -- GG carries the explicit charge to the messenger and the 'when thou hast finished telling the king' clause; CAM (v19/20 merged object) gives the 'they tell the king ... if so be' transition into the same speech.

2Sa11:20 -- and if the king's wrath arise and he say, Wherefore approached ye so nigh the city when ye fought? knew ye not they would shoot from the wall? -- both render the king's anger, the 'why came ye so nigh' rebuke and the 'knew ye not they would shoot from the wall' clause (CAM continues its merged v19/20 object here).

2Sa11:21 -- Who smote Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a millstone on him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? then say, Thy servant Uriah is dead also -- both carry the Abimelech / 'son of Roboam' (recension variant) / woman / millstone / death-at-Thebez exemplum and the 'thy servant Uriah is dead also' tag.

2Sa11:22 -- so the messenger went and came and shewed David all that Joab had sent him for -- both render the messenger's going and reporting to David; GG repeats Joab's whole Abimelech instruction as a verbatim recensional DOUBLET of the messenger's delivery (transcribed, not harmonised); CAM has the messenger speak the field report directly.

2Sa11:23 -- the messenger said, Surely the men prevailed against us and came out into the field, and we were upon them unto the entering of the gate -- both render the men prevailing, the sally into the field, the driving back to the gate (GG's tail is heavily abraded into syllable fragments but the clause is present; CAM carries it cleanly).

2Sa11:24 -- the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; some of the king's servants are dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also -- both carry the archers shooting from the wall, the dead among the king's servants and Uriah the Hittite dead also (the archery clause is on CAM's v23-object side here).

2Sa11:25 -- David said, Thus say to Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, the sword devoureth one as well as another; make thy battle stronger against the city and overthrow it; and encourage him -- both render David's reply: 'let it not be grievous', the sword-devours figure, 'press the battle against the city' and 'encourage him' (CAM 'wa-aSneʿa').
2Sa11:26 -- when the wife of Uriah heard Uriah her husband was dead she mourned for her husband -- both carry the wife of Uriah hearing of his death and mourning for her husband.

2Sa11:27 -- when the mourning was past David sent and fetched her to his house, she became his wife and bare him a son; but the thing David had done displeased the LORD -- both render the end of mourning, David fetching her, the marriage, the son and the closing 'this thing was evil before the LORD' (GG ስእግዚእ አብሐር / CAM በቅድመ እግዚእብሔር).

metrics.lacuna_counts_note: Both evidence files contain 0 ⟦illegible⟧ tokens (GG 0, CAM 0) -- the ⟦illegible⟧<->'illegible' bijection holds trivially 0<->0 in both witnesses -- so there are 0 lacuna-* rows and lacuna_counts is {gg:0,cam:0,both:0}; every alignment row is class agree or disagree only. ALIGNMENT SCHEME: the spine is the canonical 27-verse KJV 2 Sam 11 enumeration; CAM is the recommended base (cleaner / more legible / more continuous, decision D3) and its sense-objects supply the spine, but CAM writes NO red cross between the equivalents of the familiar v19 and v20 (one merged sense-object, 26 CAM objects for the 27-verse narrative) and its later objects are OFFSET from the KJV versification; CAM's offset objects are therefore SLICED onto the correct KJV spine rows by NARRATIVE CONTENT and GG's 27 sense units are likewise mapped by narrative -- never positional v==v (the CAM v19-obj feeds spine 19+20, CAM v20-obj->21, v21-obj->22, v22-obj->22/23, v23-obj->24, v24-obj->25, v25-obj->25/26, v26-obj->27). EXTENT SITUATION: unlike 1 Sam 17 (a famous short-LXX vs long-MT recensional extent split), BOTH witnesses here are the FULL/LONG Bathsheba narrative with every major beat present and 0 illegible -- so this is a genuine CLEAN-TEXT two-full-recension agreement measurement, not an extent comparison. The divergences are recensional/scribal token swaps, defective spellings, name-form variants (Eryo/Oryo, Ketyawi/Zetyawi, walde-Roboam for Jerubbesheth), CAM's v19/20 merge, a GG recensional messenger DOUBLET (Joab's Abimelech/millstone/Thebez instruction repeated near-verbatim as the messenger's report, GG vv.21-22 = ~35 one-sided GG cells), and CAM small pluses (raʾeya fedfade v2, ʾebew dittograph v11). Every one-sided cell (a token in one witness, absent-but-legible in the other) is class 'disagree' and IS counted in the (agree+disagree) aligned denominator -- recensional/scribal absence is NOT lacuna; lacuna is physical illegibility only, of which there is none. CAM was transcribed directly from the hi-res Cambridge UL MS Add. 1570 masters (no low-resolution pass for this chapter), so no delta_vs_lowres block is reported.

definitions.strict: exact literal token-string identity / (agree+disagree) aligned pairs
definitions.skeleton: diacritic/order-folded + near-homograph-folded token equality (class==agree) / (agree+disagree) aligned pairs, full aligned denominator
definitions.both_confident: skeleton-equal / aligned pairs where neither witness flagged that token uncertain or illegible (gap/insertion cells and lacuna rows also excluded from this denominator)
